==English==
{{wp|Speech disfluency}}

===Etymology 1===
{{onom|en}}.

====Pronunciation====
* {{IPA|en|/ʌm/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-um.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ʌm|s=1}} (when stressed, or as a verb)
Used in [[rhotic]] dialects. Compare to British English {{m|en|erm}}.

====Interjection====
{{en-intj}}

# {{n-g|[[expression|Expression]] of [[hesitation]], [[uncertainty]] or space [[filler]] in [[conversation]]}}.
#: {{syn|en|er|hmm|uh|eh}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Um''', I don’t know.}}
#: {{ux|en|Let’s see... '''um'''... how about this?}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2002|title=Newsweek|volume=140|page=lxxx|passage=It's a great test of the claims of open-source gurus, who say that a self-motivated community can outcode any team working for a single employer—like, '''um''', Microsoft.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2007-08-24|author=William Grimes|title=Uh, Lead My Rips: No More Bloopers|work=w:The New York Times|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2007/08/24/books/24book.html
|passage=As the years go by, speech reverts to childhood levels of disfluency, with more pauses, more errors, more repeated words, but even the peak years are not great: up to 8 percent of the average person’s word output consists of meaningless fillers and placeholders like '''um''', uh and er.|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/tERzz|archivedate=2013-01-04}}
#* {{quote-web|en|title=Baldwin Judge on FIRE!|url=http://lawofselfdefense.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/240624-Fire-Transcript.pdf|date=2024-06-24|page=2|work=Law of Self Defense|passage='''Um''' And I don't know '''um''' what to say to the court other than, I don't know how we could get through 1/5 of that.}}
# {{lb|en|chiefly|American}} {{dated spelling of|en|mmm}}.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1963|author=w:Kurt Vonnegut|title=Cat's Cradle|publisher=Dell Publishing Co., Inc.|page=65
|passage="About the same, wherever you go," he agreed.<br>"'''Um'''," I said.}}
# {{non-gloss|An expression to forcefully call attention to something wrong.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Um''', excuse me!}}
# {{lb|en|childish}} {{n-g|An expression of shocked disapproval used by a child who witnesses forbidden behavior.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2011|author=Kimberly Willis Holt|title=Piper Reed: Clubhouse Queen|page=83|passage=While I was in her room, Sam walked by and said, “'''Um''', I'm telling!”<br>“You're telling what?” I asked.<br>“You're reading Tori's journal,” she said.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2021|author=Sarah Strangeways|title=The Gingerbread House|page=13
|passage=Mair used to look after Laura. If anyone threatened to tease her, Mair would stand up straight, point her finger at the enemy and shout, ''''Um'''! I'm ''telling'' on you!'}}

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To make the ''um'' sound to express uncertainty or hesitancy.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2007|author=Michael Erard|title=Um... Slips, Stumbles, and Verbal Blunders, and What They Mean|page=136|text=Meanwhile, in the popular mind '''umming''' was simply a bad habit, akin to spitting or picking one’s nose.}}

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# An occurrence of the interjection "um".
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2007-08-24|author=William Grimes|title=Uh, Lead My Rips: No More Bloopers|work=w:The New York Times|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2007/08/24/books/24book.html
|passage=Although Shakespeare refers to “hums and ha’s,” sifting through etiquette manuals and public-speaking guides turns up scant evidence of a prohibition against '''ums''', ers and uhs, which are profuse in the first recording of Thomas Edison’s voice, in 1888. Mr. Erard, rather ingeniously, traces the prohibition on um and other speech flaws to the advent of radio in the early 1920s.|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/tERzz|archivedate=2013-01-04}}

====Alternative forms====
* {{alt|en|ahm|ehm|em|erm|hum|uhm|umm}}

===Etymology 2===
Variant form of {{m|en|-um}}.

====Particle====
{{en-part}}

# {{lb|en|dated|sometimes|humorous|often|offensive}} {{n-g|An undifferentiated determiner or article; a miscellaneous linking word, or filler with nonspecific meaning; representation of broken English stereotypically or comically attributed to Native Americans.}}
#: {{ux|en|Me be [[injun|Injun]]. Him '''um''' Growling Bear. Him '''um''' heap big chief.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1871|title=Grand camp meeting on Bear River|journal=The Keepapitchinin|page=3|text=“me heap brave—me talk to '''um''' white man so{{...}} me good injun, like '''um''' white man, ''mebbe so'', ugh!”|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=GEFOAAAAYAAJ&pg=PP3|volume=III}}

===See also===
{{col2|en|um-hum}}

===Anagrams===
* {{anagrams|en|a=mu|-mu-|MU|Mu|mu}}

==German==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|de|umb|ümb|üm||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
{{dercat|de|gem-pro|inh=1}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|umbe}}, {{m|gmh|ümbe}}, from {{inh|de|goh|umbi}}, from {{inh|de|gmw-pro|*umbi}}.

[[Central German]] dialects show regular umlaut; the standard form is from [[Upper German]], where umlaut of ''-u-'' was blocked before labial geminates and clusters. Cognate with {{cog|lb|ëm}}, {{cog|nl|om}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|de|/ʊm/}}
* {{audio|de|De-um.ogg}}
* {{audio|de|De-um3.ogg|a=<<Germany>> (<<Berlin>>)}}
* {{audio|de|De-at-um.ogg|a=Austria}}
* {{rhymes|de|ʊm}}

===Preposition===
{{head|de|preposition}} {{+obj|de|acc}}

# [[about]]
#: {{uxi|de|Es geht '''um''' den Kuchen.|It's about the pie.}}
# [[around]]
#: {{uxi|de|'''Um''' die Ecke|around the corner}}
# [[at]], [[by]] {{qual|when relating to time}}
#: {{uxi|de|'''Um''' acht Uhr reisen wir ab|At eight o’clock we depart}}
# [[by]] {{qual|percentage difference}}
#: {{uxi|de|Die Verkaufsmengen gingen '''um''' 6% zurück.|Sales in volume has decreased by 6%.}}
# {{lb|de|Austria}} [[for]] {{qual|amount of money}}
#: {{uxi|de|'''Um''' einen Euro bekommt man heute nicht besonders viel.|You can't buy much for one euro these days.}}
#: {{uxi|de|Heute im Sonderangebot '''um''' nur 99 Euro.|Special offer today for only 99 euros.}}

====Inflection====
{{de-pronadv-table|um|prep=um}}

====Derived terms====
* ('''''um''' + das'') {{l|de|ums}}

===Conjunction===
{{head|de|conjunction}} {{tlb|de|introduces a ''zu''-clause}}

# [[in order to]], [[so as to]]
#: {{ux|de|Wir sind gekommen, '''um''' zu helfen.|We’ve come ('''in order''') '''to''' help.}}

===Adjective===
{{de-adj|predonly}}

# {{lb|de|predicative|not attributive}} up, in the sense of finished
#: {{ux|de|Werden dich in kurzem binden/ [[w:Erdgeist|Erdgeist]], deine Zeit ist '''um'''|source=Friedrich von Hardenberg, ''Novalis''|We will shortly bind you/ Erdgeist, your time is up}}

===Adverb===
{{de-adv}}

# [[around]], [[about]]
# turned over, [[changed]], from one state to another

====Derived terms====
{{col3|de|um meinetwillen|um euretwillen|um Ihretwillen|um deinetwillen|um ihretwillen|um seinetwillen}}

==Icelandic==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|is|umb}}

===Etymology===
{{inh+|is|non|um}}, {{inh+|is|gem-pro|*umbi<t:around, about>|nocap=1}}.

===Adverb===
{{is-adv}}

# {{ng|used in set phrases}}
#: {{ux|is|Það er [[um að gera|'''um''' að gera]] að sofa vel.|The important thing to do is to sleep well.}}
#: {{ux|is|Hvað er '''um''' að vera?|What's going on?}}
#: {{ux|is|Eins og '''um''' var talað.|As was agreed.}}

====Derived terms====
* {{l|is|um að gera}}
* {{l|is|vera um og ó}}

===Preposition===
{{head|is|preposition}} {{+obj|is|acc}}

# [[about]], [[concerning]]
#: {{ux|is|'''Um''' hvað ertu að tala?|What are you talking '''about'''?}}
#: {{ux|is|Spurning '''um''' líf og dauða.|A question '''of''' life and death.}}
# [[through]], [[around]], [[across]]
#: {{ux|is|Áin rennur '''um''' dalinn.|The river runs '''through''' the valley.}}
#: {{ux|is|Að fara út '''um''' gluggann.|To go out '''through''' the window.}}
#: {{ux|is|Vestur '''um''' haf.|West '''across''' the sea.}}
# [[throughout]], [[over]], [[around]]
#: {{ux|is|Við förum '''um''' alla sveitina.|We'll go '''throughout''' the district.}}
#: {{ux|is|Hann var breiður '''um''' herðar.|He was broad '''across''' the shoulders.}}
#: {{ux|is|Hún hafði klút '''um''' hálsinn.|She had a scarf '''around''' her neck.}}
# [[during]], [[for]], [[in]], [[at]]
#: {{ux|is|Hvenær gerðist þetta?'' - ''Þetta gerðist '''um''' sumarið.|When did this happen? - It happened '''during''' the summer.}}
#: {{ux|is|Ég fór '''um''' nóttina.|I went '''during''' the night.}}
# [[approximately]], [[about]], [[around]]
#: {{ux|is|Pokinn er '''um''' fjögur kíló.|The bag is '''around''' four kilos.}}

====Usage notes====
* Often used with phrases such as "''[[brjóta heilann]] '''um'''''".
*: {{ux|is|Ég er búinn að [[brjóta heilann]] '''um''' þetta alla nótt!|I've been racking my brain '''about''' this all night!}}

===Article===

#: {{uxi|pt|'''Um''' carro, '''uma''' casa.|'''A''' car, '''a''' house.}}

#* {{RQ:mul:Rowling Harry Potter|pt-BR|6|page=361|text={{...}} disse o professor com '''um''' sorrisinho {{...}}|t={{...}} the teacher said with a little smile {{...}}}}
## {{senseid|pt|plural article}} {{lb|pt|in the plural}} [[some]]; [[a few]] {{gloss|a small number of}}
##: {{uxi|pt|'''Uns''' carros, '''umas''' casas.|'''A few''' cars, '''a few''' houses.}}
##: {{syn|pt|alguns}}
## {{senseid|pt|a bit of}} {{lb|pt|with uncountable nouns}} [[a bit]] of
##: {{syn|pt|um pouco de}}
## {{senseid|pt|quite a}} {{lb|pt|usually in the feminine|pronounced slowly, emphatically and with a high intonation}} {{n-g|indicates that what follows is exceptional}}; [[quite]] a; [[quite]] the
##: {{ux|pt|Ontem de noite caiu '''''uma''''' chuva.|We had '''quite a''' rain last night.}}
##: {{ux|pt|Estamos comendo '''''um''''' churrasco.|We are having '''''the''''' barbecue.}}
##: {{syn|pt|aquele}}
